organization_parameters.I: Approved human/workload principals, role scopes, separation of duties, privileged elevation duration, access review frequency, emergency accounts and permitted authentication methods.
organization_parameters.N: Approved ingress/egress and service destinations, public exposure exceptions, allowed client networks, private subresources and network-team evidence owner.
organization_parameters.R: Classified information/storage boundaries, required confidentiality/integrity mechanisms and approved cryptography. Provider-managed keys are accepted; CMK is conditional on an explicit separate requirement.
organization_parameters.T: Approved protocols and minimum versions, certificate validation/trust and any protocol-specific exceptions; propose TLS 1.2 or stronger where supported, subject to approved architecture.
organization_parameters.K: Credential/certificate/key lifetime, rotation and revocation periods, approved issuers/algorithms, expiry warning threshold, custody and recovery requirements.
organization_parameters.L: Required event categories/content, retention by dataset, clock accuracy, maximum ingestion lag/missing-event window, capacity threshold, destination protection and review frequency.
organization_parameters.C: Approved baseline/version, change approval and emergency change process, drift interval/tolerance, permitted features, exception approver and expiry.
organization_parameters.V: Supported version policy, scan scope/frequency/freshness, severity-based remediation deadlines, trusted publishers/digests and compensating-control approval.
organization_parameters.B: BIA-derived RPO/RTO, backup frequency/retention/isolation, integrity checks, restore-test interval and success measures, availability/capacity requirements.
organization_parameters.O: Authoritative tenant/subscription/service inventory, named accountable owners, classification, region/retention rules, lifecycle states and reconciliation frequency.
organization_parameters.D: Threat scenarios, detection coverage and test frequency, triage/notification/containment deadlines, responders, evidence preservation and exercise cadence.
organization_parameters.G: Selected NIST baseline/tailoring and assessment depth/coverage, control owners, evidence age/sampling, legal/privacy basis, supplier assurance, exception and risk acceptance periods.

families.title: Access Control
families.review: Resource and data-plane access, IAM lifecycle, inherited/group/conditional rights, workload trust and periodic removal decisions. AC-7/8/11/12 and mobile/wireless/public-content controls are assessed where actual human-facing applications/endpoints exist; they are not fabricated as Azure switches.

families.title: Awareness and Training
families.review: Awareness, role-specific training and completion records for cloud/IAM/network/SOC/backup operators. No resource property proves competence or training attendance. Specialized exercises follow selected roles and threats.

families.title: Audit and Accountability
families.review: Event selection/generation, content, storage/retention, health, integrity and operating review. Session recording/non-repudiation/cross-organization sharing enhancements require an actual use case and explicit selection; enabling diagnostics does not satisfy them.

families.title: Assessment, Authorization, and Monitoring
families.review: Assessment scope/independence, system exchanges, authorization, corrective actions and continuous monitoring; authorized penetration test records when selected. Resource inventory cannot authorize a system or prove all interconnection agreements.

families.title: Configuration Management
families.review: Baselines, approved changes, restricted writers, drift, component/data-location inventory and signed artifacts. Software licensing/user-installation controls apply to VM/AKS/app/worker software; SaaS host software is a provider responsibility.

families.title: Contingency Planning
families.review: BIA, plans/training, alternate storage/processing/telecom as required, protected backups and measured restoration. Stateless constructs can use tested rebuild; this excludes data-backup mechanics only with documented dependency scope.

families.title: Identification and Authentication
families.review: Human identity/MFA, workload identities, credential lifecycle and identity-provider trust. Machine identities do not use human MFA. Identity proofing and reauthentication come from tenant/app policies and evidence; biometric/PIV requirements are conditional, not assumed.

families.title: Incident Response
families.review: Detection/triage/containment/reporting, exercises, support and spill response for classified data. Alert existence alone proves none of the full operating process. Provider incident notices supplement customer incident records.

families.title: Maintenance
families.review: Provider facilities/platform maintenance inherited with assurance; VM/worker remote maintenance, tools, authorization and personnel are customer duties. Physical field maintenance is conditional on owned/hybrid equipment.

families.title: Media Protection
families.review: Physical disk custody/sanitization inherited only in Azure boundary. Exported backups/reports/removable media and local audit archives need access/storage/transport/disposal controls. Deleting a resource is not proof of physical media sanitization.

families.title: Physical and Environmental Protection
families.review: Datacenter access, visitors, power/fire/environment and facility location inherited through assurance. Hybrid workers/admin workstations/customer sites stay customer owned. Specialized electromagnetic/leakage controls need threat/classification selection.

families.title: Planning
families.review: System/security/privacy plans, rules of behavior, architecture, common controls, selected baseline and tailoring. Service list is a boundary input, not approval of an 800-53B baseline or organization-defined values.

families.title: Program Management
families.review: Program accountability/resources, risk strategy, privacy governance, supplier strategy and continuous-monitoring strategy need enterprise records. National-security, federal reporting and specific program controls depend on organization obligations.

families.title: Personnel Security
families.review: Screening, position risk, agreements, transfers/termination, external personnel and sanctions. Correlate joiner/mover/leaver records to rights removal without collecting unnecessary HR data. Provider workforce evidence is inherited.

families.title: Personally Identifiable Information Processing and Transparency
families.review: Authority, purpose, consent/notices and special PII processing. PT-6 federal system-of-records notices and PT-8 matching requirements are conditional legal determinations. No PII/no federal duty exclusions require a documented data/obligations review, including telemetry.

families.title: Risk Assessment
families.review: Classification, threat/impact/criticality, privacy assessments, fresh scoped vulnerability evidence and risk treatment. Threat hunting requires operational evidence where selected. Physical surveillance surveys are not automatic cloud configuration checks.

families.title: System and Services Acquisition
families.review: Contracts, service responsibilities, documentation, secure SDLC/testing and supported components. Criticality can justify resilient design; new logging/resiliency controls are candidates, not retroactive mandates. Formal methods/source review of provider internals require assurance evidence, not guesses.

families.title: System and Communications Protection
families.review: At-rest/transit protection, key/certificate lifecycle, service boundaries and availability. DNS/routing architecture belongs to network owner; application session authenticity/process isolation to app/platform; physical/EM/covert-channel enhancements require actual selected threat scope.

families.title: System and Information Integrity
families.review: Flaws/malware, integrity, advisories, monitoring, input/error handling, retention/privacy and customer memory protection where relevant. No managed-service metadata can establish application input validation or provider firmware integrity; tests/assurance needed.

families.title: Supply Chain Risk Management
families.responsibility: Procurement, provider and software supply chain
families.review: Supplier risks/reviews, notification, provenance, authenticity and disposal for images/modules/SDKs and cloud vendors. Hardware inspection/tamper controls inherited for provider equipment, direct for owned hardware if selected. SBOM presence is not supplier trust or remediation.
